item.body:
### Summary

As a member writing a reply, I want the text I type to be the same size as the messages I read, so that switching between reading and writing is not jarring. Operator feedback (device, 2026-11-13): the font in the input area is smaller than in the reading area, which is disturbing; it should be consistent.

### Where the two sizes come from (read from `dev-swift`; cause to confirm)
- **Reader:** `App/SwiftHFR/Reader/Resources/reader.css:58-62`. The base is `font: -apple-system-body` (Dynamic Type) times `--text-scale`, the in-app text size of LOT-169 (`GeneralSettingsModel.textSizePercent`, the app-wide type scale).
- **Composer:** `App/SwiftHFR/Composer/ComposerEditorCard.swift:59`, SwiftUI's `TextEditor` with no explicit font, so the default body style. Does it get the LOT-169 scale? Check first: if it does not, any in-app text size above 100 % makes the reader larger than the editor.
- Check also any other cause, such as a different text style or a fixed size somewhere in the editor's environment.

### Scope
- The editor's text uses the same size as the reader's message text: the same Dynamic Type base and the same in-app scale (LOT-169), and it follows both live.
- The composer's chrome (buttons, title) is not in scope: only the typed text.
- Mind the card height: `ComposerCardLayout` measures the text, so the six-line cap and the XL two-line rule must still hold (#854 is reworking this card).

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At the in-app sizes 80 %, 100 % and 150 %, and with Dynamic Type default and XL, the typed text and the reader's message text have the same point size.
- [ ] A test pins the editor's font against the reader's scale rule.
- [ ] Card height rules unchanged (existing tests green).

Related: LOT-169 (in-app text size), #854 (composer chrome), #853 (inline composer bar).
